senses.def: the fact of people living in a place
ex: The house is not fit for habitation.
There were signs of human habitation.

senses.def: to get into someone else's computer system without permission
ex: Someone hacked into the company's files.
His email account was hacked.

senses.def: to cut something roughly with a tool
ex: They hacked a path through the jungle.

senses.def: a clever trick that makes something easier
ex: She shared a useful life hack.

senses.def: past form of have: owned or experienced
ex: I had a small dog.
We had a great time.

senses.def: used with a past participle to form the past perfect
ex: She had finished before I arrived.

mistake.note: After had, use the past participle (gone), not the past simple (went).

senses.def: to call or wave to attract someone's attention
ex: He hailed a taxi.
She hailed a passing bus.

senses.def: to describe someone or something as very good
ex: The film was hailed as a masterpiece.

senses.def: the thin threads that grow on your head
ex: She has long black hair.
I need to wash my hair.

mistake.note: For the hair on the head, hair is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

senses.def: a person whose job is to cut and style hair
ex: I have an appointment at the hairdresser's.
My hairdresser cut it short.

senses.def: covered with a lot of hair
ex: He has hairy arms.
The spider was big and hairy.

senses.def: one of two equal parts of something
ex: Cut the apple in half.
The second half of the game was exciting.

senses.def: 50 per cent of something
ex: Half the class was absent.
I waited half an hour.

senses.def: 50 per cent of a number or amount
ex: Half of them are my friends.

senses.def: partly; not completely
ex: The glass is half empty.
I was half asleep.

mistake.note: Say half an hour; the article comes after half.

senses.def: a tool with a heavy metal head used for hitting nails
ex: He hit the nail with a hammer.
Pass me the hammer.

senses.def: to hit something with a hammer, or hit hard and repeatedly
ex: He hammered the nail into the wall.
Rain hammered on the roof.

senses.def: to make it difficult for someone to do something
ex: Bad weather hampered the rescue.
Lack of money hampers our work.

senses.def: the part of the body at the end of the arm
ex: Wash your hands.
She held a pen in her hand.

senses.def: help
ex: Can you give me a hand?

senses.def: to give something to someone with your hand
ex: Please hand me the salt.
She handed him a letter.

senses.def: something that makes it harder for you to do something
ex: Not speaking the language was a big handicap.
Shyness can be a handicap at interviews.

senses.def: a small piece of cloth used for wiping your nose or eyes
ex: He wiped his face with a handkerchief.
She kept a handkerchief in her pocket.

senses.def: the part of an object that you hold
ex: The door handle is broken.
Hold the cup by the handle.

senses.def: to deal with a situation or problem
ex: She handled the problem well.
Can you handle this job?

senses.def: to touch, hold or use something with your hands
ex: Handle the glass with care.

senses.def: the way a person writes with a pen or pencil
ex: Your handwriting is very neat.
I can't read his handwriting.

senses.def: useful and easy to use
ex: A torch is handy when the lights go out.
This is a handy little tool.

senses.def: near and easy to reach
ex: Keep a pen handy.

senses.def: to attach something at the top so the bottom is free
ex: She hung her coat on the hook.
A picture hangs on the wall.

senses.def: get the hang of: to learn how to do something
ex: I'm starting to get the hang of this game.

senses.def: fixed at the top so that the bottom is free
ex: The hotel has a hanging garden.
A hanging lamp lit the room.

senses.def: the killing of a person by hanging them with a rope
ex: The law bans hanging.

senses.def: without any plan or order
ex: Books were piled in a haphazard way.
Her filing system is haphazard.

senses.def: unlucky and deserving pity
ex: The hapless tourist lost his passport.
A hapless driver got stuck in the mud.

senses.def: to take place, especially without being planned
ex: What happened to you?
The accident happened on Monday.

senses.def: to do something by chance
ex: I happened to be there.

mistake.note: happen is never used in the passive.

senses.def: the feeling of being happy
ex: Money cannot buy happiness.
Her face shone with happiness.

senses.def: feeling or showing pleasure
ex: I'm very happy today.
She looked happy.

senses.def: satisfied that something is good or right
ex: Are you happy with your new phone?

senses.def: to keep annoying or threatening someone
ex: He was harassed by journalists.
Workers should not be harassed at work.

senses.def: behaviour that annoys or upsets someone, often repeated
ex: She complained of harassment at work.
The law protects people from harassment.

senses.def: an area of water next to land where ships can stay safe
ex: Boats were tied up in the harbour.
We walked along the harbour.

senses.def: to keep a thought or feeling in your mind for a long time
ex: He harboured a grudge against his boss.

senses.def: firm and solid; not soft
ex: The bed was very hard.
The ground is hard in winter.

senses.def: difficult to do or understand
ex: This exercise is hard.
It's hard to say goodbye.

senses.def: with a lot of effort or force
ex: She works hard.
It was raining hard.

mistake.note: hardly means 'almost not'; the adverb of hard is hard.

senses.def: almost not; only just
ex: I could hardly breathe.
He hardly ever calls me.

mistake.note: hardly is already negative, so do not use it with not.

senses.def: the physical parts of a computer
ex: We need to upgrade our computer hardware.
The shop sells hardware and software.

senses.def: tools and equipment for the house and garden
ex: He bought nails at the hardware store.

senses.def: to hurt or damage someone or something
ex: Smoking can harm your health.
The dog would never harm a child.

senses.def: damage or injury
ex: The storm did no harm.
There's no harm in asking.

senses.def: not able or likely to cause damage or injury
ex: The snake is harmless.
It was a harmless joke.

senses.def: a set of straps used to hold a person or control an animal
ex: The climber wore a safety harness.
The horse wore a leather harness.

senses.def: the form of 'have' used with he, she and it
ex: She has two brothers.
He has a new phone.

senses.def: used with a past participle to make the present perfect tense
ex: He has finished his homework.

senses.def: great speed in doing something, often too much, because you have little time
ex: In his haste, he left his keys at home.
Decisions made in haste are often wrong.

senses.def: done too quickly, without thinking carefully
ex: Don't make a hasty decision.
They made a hasty exit from the room.

senses.def: a small door or opening in a floor, ceiling, ship or aircraft
ex: He climbed up through the hatch into the attic.

senses.def: to dislike someone or something very much
ex: I hate waiting in long queues.
She hates it when people are late.

senses.def: a very strong feeling of dislike for someone or something
ex: He looked at them with hate in his eyes.

senses.def: a very strong feeling of dislike for someone or something
ex: There is no place for hatred in our school.
Her hatred of lies is well known.

senses.def: proud and acting as if you are better than other people
ex: She gave him a haughty look and walked away.
His haughty manner annoyed everyone.

senses.def: a place that someone often visits
ex: The café was a favourite haunt of local artists.

senses.def: if a ghost haunts a place, it appears there often
ex: People say a ghost haunts the old castle.

senses.def: to cause worry or sadness for a long time
ex: The accident still haunts him years later.

senses.def: beautiful or sad in a way that stays in your mind
ex: The film has a haunting soundtrack.
She sang a haunting melody.

senses.def: used with a past participle to make perfect tenses
ex: I have seen that film twice.
They have already left.

senses.def: to own or hold something, or to experience or possess a feature
ex: We have a small garden.
She has long dark hair.

mistake.note: Do not use 'have' in the continuous form when it means 'own'.

senses.def: a place where people or animals are safe and calm
ex: The garden was a haven of peace.
The park is a haven for wildlife.

senses.def: long dry grass that is cut and used to feed animals
ex: The farmer stored hay in the barn for winter.

senses.def: something that may cause danger or harm
ex: Smoking is a serious health hazard.
Wet floors are a hazard for workers.

senses.def: to say something that may be wrong, as a guess
ex: I'll hazard a guess that he is late again.

senses.def: used for a man, boy or male animal that has already been mentioned
ex: My brother is a doctor. He works at night.
Where is Tom? He is outside.

senses.def: the part of the body above the neck that has the brain, eyes and mouth
ex: She shook her head.
He hit his head on the door.

senses.def: the person in charge of a group or organisation
ex: She is the head of the school.

senses.def: to go in a particular direction
ex: We headed home after the match.
The ship is heading north.

senses.def: the title of a newspaper story, printed in large letters
ex: The headline said the team had won.
I only read the headlines this morning.

senses.def: a woman who is in charge of a school
ex: The headmistress welcomed the new pupils.
She became headmistress at the age of forty.

senses.def: the main office of a company or organisation
ex: The company's headquarters is in Dubai.
Police headquarters are in the city centre.

senses.def: determined to do what you want and not listening to advice
ex: She was a headstrong child who never listened.
His headstrong nature caused many arguments.

senses.def: to become healthy again, or to make someone or something healthy again
ex: The cut took a week to heal.
Time heals many wounds.

senses.def: helping someone or something to become healthy again
ex: Rest has a healing effect on the body.
Many people believe in the healing power of nature.

senses.def: an untidy pile of things
ex: There was a heap of clothes on the floor.
He threw the rubbish onto the heap.

senses.def: to put things in a large pile
ex: She heaped food onto his plate.

senses.def: to notice a sound with your ears
ex: I can't hear you very well.
Did you hear that noise?

senses.def: to be told information or news
ex: I heard that she is moving to Cairo.

mistake.note: 'Hear' means to notice a sound; use 'listen to' when you pay attention on purpose.

senses.def: the ability to hear sounds
ex: My grandfather's hearing is getting worse.

senses.def: a meeting in a court or official group where facts are listened to
ex: The hearing will take place next Tuesday.

senses.def: the organ in your chest that sends blood around your body
ex: His heart was beating fast.
She has a weak heart.

senses.def: the place where your deepest feelings are thought to be
ex: She has a kind heart.

senses.def: the central or most important part of something
ex: The hotel is in the heart of the city.

senses.def: the quality of being hot, or a high temperature
ex: I can't stand the heat in summer.
Cook it over a low heat.

senses.def: to make something warm or hot, or to become warm
ex: Heat the soup for two minutes.
The house heats up quickly.

senses.def: the place where some people believe good people go after they die
ex: Many people hope to go to heaven.

senses.def: a very pleasant place or situation
ex: This beach is heaven on earth.

senses.def: very pleasant or beautiful
ex: The cake tasted heavenly.
What a heavenly view!

senses.def: in large amounts or to a great degree
ex: It rained heavily all night.
He drinks heavily.

senses.def: in a slow way that shows something is heavy
ex: He sat down heavily on the sofa.

senses.def: a line of bushes planted close together, often around a garden or field
ex: He cut the hedge on Saturday.
Our garden has a high hedge.

senses.def: a small brown animal with sharp spines on its back
ex: A hedgehog rolled into a ball when we came near.

senses.def: the back part of the foot below the ankle
ex: I have a blister on my heel.

senses.def: the raised part at the back of a shoe
ex: She wore shoes with high heels.

senses.def: how tall someone or something is
ex: The tower is 300 metres in height.
What is your height?

senses.def: the highest or strongest point of something
ex: She was at the height of her fame.

mistake.note: We say 'tall' for people, and 'high' for things, and do not add 'long' after the height.

senses.def: an aircraft with long blades on top that spin and lift it into the air
ex: A helicopter landed on the roof of the hospital.
They rescued him by helicopter.

senses.def: the place where some people believe bad people go after they die
ex: He believed that bad people would go to hell.

senses.def: a very unpleasant experience
ex: The journey was hell.

senses.def: a word you say when you meet someone or answer the phone
ex: Hello, how are you?
Say hello to your sister.

senses.def: the wheel or handle used to steer a ship
ex: The captain stood at the helm.

senses.def: the position of being in charge
ex: The company did well with her at the helm.

senses.def: a hard hat that protects your head
ex: You must wear a helmet when you ride a bike.

senses.def: to do something useful for someone so that their work is easier
ex: Can you help me with my bag?
She helps her mother in the kitchen.

senses.def: to improve a situation or make it better
ex: Cold water will help the pain.

senses.def: the act of helping someone
ex: Thank you for your help.
Do you need any help?

mistake.note: 'Help' is uncountable in this sense, so it has no plural.

senses.def: a person who helps someone to do a job
ex: The teacher asked for a helper to carry the books.
She works as a helper in the nursery.

senses.def: not able to look after yourself or do anything to change a bad situation
ex: He felt helpless as he watched the fire.
A baby is completely helpless.

senses.def: for this reason
ex: The prices are low, hence the large crowds.
She was ill, hence her absence.

senses.def: from this time
ex: Two years hence, the road will be finished.

senses.def: belonging to or connected with a woman or girl already mentioned
ex: Maria loves her job.
Her car is blue.

senses.def: used for a woman or girl as the object of a verb or preposition
ex: I saw her yesterday.
Give the book to her.

senses.def: to be a sign that something is about to happen
ex: The new law heralds a major change.

senses.def: a sign that something is going to happen
ex: The first flowers are a herald of spring.

senses.def: a plant used to add flavour to food or as medicine
ex: Add fresh herbs to the soup.
Mint is a common herb.

senses.def: a large group of animals of the same kind that live together
ex: A herd of cows crossed the road.
We saw a herd of elephants.

senses.def: in or to this place
ex: Come here, please.
I live here.

senses.def: used when you give something to someone
ex: Here is your ticket.

senses.def: the traditions, buildings and values that a country has had for a long time
ex: The old town is part of our national heritage.
They are proud of their cultural heritage.

senses.def: a person who chooses to live alone, away from other people
ex: The old man lived like a hermit in the mountains.

senses.def: a person who is admired for doing something brave or good
ex: The firefighter became a local hero.
He is my childhood hero.

senses.def: the main male character in a story, film or play
ex: The hero of the film is a young teacher.

senses.def: a woman who is admired for doing something brave or good
ex: She was a heroine to many young girls.

senses.def: the main female character in a story, film or play
ex: The heroine of the novel is a doctor.

senses.def: used when a woman or girl does something to her own self
ex: She hurt herself playing football.
Anna made herself a sandwich.

senses.def: used to stress that a woman did something without help
ex: She painted the room herself.

senses.def: to wait before doing or saying something because you are not sure
ex: She hesitated before answering the question.
Don't hesitate to call me.

senses.def: a pause before you do or say something because you are not sure
ex: He answered without hesitation.
There was a moment of hesitation.

senses.def: used to get someone's attention, or to say hello in a friendly way
ex: Hey, wait for me!
Hey, how are you doing?

senses.def: a friendly word you say when you meet someone
ex: Hi, Sam! How are you?
She said hi and smiled.

senses.def: a long sleep that some animals have during the winter
ex: Bears go into hibernation in autumn.

senses.def: not easy to see or find
ex: They found a hidden door behind the shelf.
The village is hidden in the mountains.

senses.def: measuring a large distance from bottom to top
ex: The wall is very high.
It is a high mountain.

senses.def: large in amount, level or strength
ex: The shop has high prices.

senses.def: at or to a great height
ex: The bird flew high above the trees.

mistake.right: He is a very tall man.
mistake.note: Use 'tall' for people and 'high' for things such as buildings, mountains or prices.

senses.def: using the newest and most advanced technology
ex: She works for a high-tech company.
The hospital has high-tech equipment.

senses.def: to a high degree; very
ex: It is highly unlikely that it will rain.
He is a highly skilled worker.

senses.def: in a way that shows you admire someone or something
ex: Everyone speaks highly of her.

senses.def: extremely funny
ex: The film was absolutely hilarious.
He told us a hilarious story.

senses.def: used for a man or boy as the object of a verb or preposition
ex: I know him well.
Please give this to him.

senses.def: used when a man or boy does something to his own self
ex: He cut himself with a knife.
Tom bought himself a watch.

senses.def: used to stress that a man did something without help
ex: He fixed the car himself.

senses.def: to make it difficult for something to happen or develop
ex: Bad weather hindered the rescue.
Poor health hindered his progress.

senses.def: something or someone that makes it harder to do something
ex: Heavy snow was a hindrance to the rescue team.

senses.def: understanding of an event only after it has happened
senses.ar: النظرة المتأخّرة؛ إدراك بعد وقوع الحدث
ex: With hindsight, I should have said no.

senses.def: something you say or do to show what you mean without saying it directly
ex: He dropped a hint about the party.
She took the hint and left.

senses.def: a very small amount of something
ex: There was a hint of sadness in her voice.

senses.def: a small piece of useful advice
ex: Here are some hints for new learners.

senses.def: the part at each side of your body between the waist and the leg
ex: She put her hands on her hips.
He broke his hip in the fall.

senses.def: to pay someone to work for you
ex: The company hired ten new workers.
They hired a lawyer.

senses.def: to pay to use something for a short time
ex: We hired a car for the weekend.

mistake.wrong: I hired a house for one year and paid every month.
mistake.right: I rented a house for one year.
mistake.note: In British English 'hire' is for short periods, while 'rent' is for longer periods like a house or flat.

senses.def: belonging to or connected with a man or boy already mentioned
ex: John loves his dog.
His house is big.

senses.def: the one that belongs to a man or boy
ex: This bag is his.
Mine is red and his is blue.

senses.def: important or famous in history
ex: It was a historic day for the country.
We visited a historic castle.

mistake.wrong: We read a historic book about Egypt.
mistake.right: We read a historical book about Egypt.
mistake.note: 'Historic' means important in history, while 'historical' means connected with the past.

senses.def: connected with the past or with the study of history
ex: She reads historical novels.
We found historical evidence of the old city.

senses.def: to touch something quickly and hard with your hand or an object
ex: He hit the ball over the fence.
The car hit a tree.

senses.def: something, such as a song or film, that is very popular
ex: The song was a big hit last summer.

senses.def: a visit to a website
ex: The page got a thousand hits in one day.

senses.def: to fasten something to something else with a hook or rope
ex: He hitched the trailer to the back of the car.

senses.def: to get a free ride in someone's car
ex: She hitched a ride to the city.

senses.def: until this time
ex: The disease was hitherto unknown in this region.

senses.def: to lift something heavy, often using ropes or a machine
ex: They hoisted the flag at dawn.
He hoisted the box onto his shoulder.

senses.def: the act of holding something with your hands
ex: Keep a firm hold of the rope.
She took hold of my hand.

senses.def: to have something in your hands or arms
ex: She was holding a baby.
Hold my hand.

senses.def: to have space for a certain amount or number
ex: The stadium holds 50,000 people.

senses.def: to arrange and have an event
ex: The meeting will be held on Friday.

senses.def: a person who has or owns something such as a ticket or licence
ex: Ticket holders can enter through this door.
She is the holder of a world record.

senses.def: an object that holds or supports something
ex: He put the pens in a holder.

senses.def: with an empty space inside
ex: The tree trunk was hollow.
Chocolate eggs are usually hollow.

senses.def: without real feeling or value
ex: His promise sounded hollow.

senses.def: the killing of very large numbers of people, especially during a war
ex: The museum tells the story of the Holocaust.
A nuclear holocaust would destroy the world.

senses.def: connected with God or a religion, and treated with great respect
ex: Mecca is a holy city.
Many people visit holy places each year.

senses.def: the house or place where you live
ex: I stayed at home all day.
She left home at eighteen.

senses.def: to the place where you live
ex: I'm going home now.
He came home late.

mistake.wrong: I went to home after school.
mistake.note: Do not use 'to' before 'home' when it is an adverb of direction.

senses.def: having no place to live
ex: The fire left many families homeless.
The charity helps homeless people.

senses.def: simple, warm and comfortable, like a home
ex: The small hotel has a homely atmosphere.

senses.def: a farm and the buildings around it
ex: The family lived on a remote homestead.

senses.def: telling the truth and not cheating or stealing
ex: Please be honest with me.
He is an honest man.

senses.def: in a way that tells the truth
ex: Answer the question honestly.
I honestly don't know.

senses.def: used to show you are annoyed or surprised
ex: Honestly, you are always late!

senses.def: the quality of being honest
ex: I admire her honesty.
Honesty is important in a friendship.

senses.def: a sweet, sticky food made by bees
ex: I put honey on my toast.
She added a spoon of honey to her tea.

senses.def: a holiday taken by two people who have just got married
ex: They went to Italy for their honeymoon.

senses.def: to make a short loud sound with a car horn
ex: Drivers honked their horns in the traffic.

senses.def: a short loud sound made by a car horn or a goose
ex: We heard a loud honk behind us.

senses.def: great respect and admiration, or a reason to feel proud
ex: It is an honor to meet you.
He received the award with honor.

senses.def: to show great respect for someone or something in public
ex: The city honored the soldiers with a parade.

senses.def: to do what you have promised or agreed
ex: The company honored the agreement.

senses.def: honest and deserving respect
ex: He was an honorable man.
It was an honorable thing to do.

senses.def: a part of a coat that you pull up to cover your head
ex: She pulled up her hood because of the rain.

senses.def: the metal cover over the engine of a car (US)
ex: He opened the hood to check the engine.

senses.def: a curved piece of metal or plastic used for hanging or catching things
ex: He hung his coat on the hook.
The fish was caught on a hook.

senses.def: to fasten or hang something using a hook
ex: She hooked the bag over her arm.

senses.def: a short jump on one foot, or a quick jump by a small animal
ex: The rabbit gave a little hop.

senses.def: a short journey, especially by plane
ex: It's only a short hop to Dubai.

senses.def: a feeling of wanting something good to happen
ex: I have no hope of winning.
There is hope for the future.

senses.def: to want something to happen or be true
ex: I hope you feel better soon.
We are hoping for good weather.

senses.def: used to say that you hope something will happen
ex: Hopefully, it won't rain tomorrow.
Hopefully we'll arrive before dark.

senses.def: with no hope of success or improvement
ex: The situation seemed hopeless.
It's hopeless to argue with him.

senses.def: very bad at something
ex: I'm hopeless at cooking.

senses.def: the line in the distance where the sky seems to meet the land or sea
ex: The sun disappeared below the horizon.
A ship appeared on the horizon.

senses.def: the range of things you know about or are interested in
ex: Travelling widens your horizons.

senses.def: one of the hard pointed parts on the head of some animals
ex: The bull lowered its horns.

senses.def: a device in a vehicle that makes a loud warning sound
ex: He pressed the horn to warn the cyclist.

senses.def: very unpleasant or bad
ex: The weather was horrible.
What a horrible smell!

senses.def: friendly and generous treatment of guests
ex: Thank you for your kind hospitality.
Arab hospitality is famous around the world.

senses.def: the business of providing food, drink and places to stay
ex: She works in the hospitality industry.

senses.def: a woman who invites people to a party or meal and looks after them

senses.def: unfriendly or ready to fight
ex: The crowd was hostile to the speaker.
He gave me a hostile look.

senses.def: difficult or unpleasant for living or growing
ex: Plants cannot grow in such a hostile environment.

senses.def: angry and unfriendly behaviour towards someone
ex: There was open hostility between the two groups.
She faced hostility from her neighbours.

senses.def: having a high temperature
ex: It's very hot today.
Be careful, the tea is hot.

senses.def: having a strong, burning taste from spices
ex: I don't like hot food.

senses.def: a period of 60 minutes
ex: The film is two hours long.
I'll be back in an hour.

mistake.note: 'Hour' means a length of time, while the clock time is told with 'o'clock'.

senses.def: a building where people live, usually for one family
ex: They live in a big house.
Our house has a small garden.

senses.def: to provide a place to live or be kept
ex: The building houses over 200 students.
The museum houses a famous painting.

senses.def: all the people who live together in one home
ex: There are five people in our household.

senses.def: a person whose job is to clean and look after a house or hotel

senses.def: a woman who stays at home to look after her family and does not have a paid job
ex: My grandmother was a housewife all her life.

senses.def: used to ask about the way something is done
ex: How do you make this soup?
How did you get here?

senses.def: used with 'much' or 'many' to ask about amount, or with adjectives to ask about degree
ex: How old are you?
How much is this?

mistake.note: In questions, the verb comes before the subject after 'how'.

senses.def: used to introduce a statement that contrasts with something just said
ex: Cars are convenient. However, they pollute the air.

senses.def: in whatever way or to whatever degree
ex: However hard I try, I can't remember her name.

mistake.wrong: Cars are convenient, however they pollute the air.
mistake.right: Cars are convenient. However, they pollute the air. / Cars are convenient; however, they pollute the air.
mistake.note: however is not a conjunction like but. Start a new sentence or use a semicolon.

senses.def: to move close together, usually because of cold or fear
ex: The children huddled around the fire.
We huddled under one umbrella.

senses.def: a small group of people standing close together
ex: A huddle of tourists waited in the rain.

senses.def: to put your arms around someone to show love or friendship
ex: She hugged her mother goodbye.
The two friends hugged.

senses.def: the act of holding someone tightly in your arms
ex: He gave his daughter a big hug.

senses.def: extremely large in size or amount
ex: They live in a huge house.
The film was a huge success.

senses.def: the main body of a ship
ex: Water leaked through a hole in the hull.

senses.def: relating to or typical of people
ex: The human body is mostly water.
It is only human to make mistakes.

senses.def: a person
ex: Humans have lived here for thousands of years.

senses.def: showing kindness and care towards people or animals
ex: The prisoners deserve humane treatment.
Is this a humane way to treat animals?

senses.def: all people in the world, thought of as a group
ex: The disease is a threat to humanity.
Pollution affects all of humanity.

senses.def: kind and fair treatment of other people
ex: She treated everyone with humanity.

senses.def: not thinking that you are better than other people
ex: Despite his success, he remained humble.
She gave a humble apology.

senses.def: simple and not rich or important
ex: He came from a humble family.

senses.def: to make someone feel less proud or important
ex: The defeat humbled the champion.

senses.def: to make someone feel embarrassed and lose respect in front of others
ex: He humiliated her in front of her colleagues.
I felt humiliated by the comment.

senses.def: making you feel ashamed and embarrassed
ex: It was a humiliating defeat for the team.
Losing the job was humiliating.

senses.def: the feeling of being made to look stupid or being ashamed in front of others
ex: He could not hide his humiliation.
The loss was a public humiliation.

senses.def: the quality of being funny, or the ability to enjoy funny things
ex: She has a great sense of humor.
I like British humor.

senses.def: the number 100
ex: The tickets cost a hundred pounds.
Two hundred people came.

mistake.note: After a number, 'hundred' has no -s; use 'hundreds of' only when you do not give a number.

senses.def: the feeling you have when you need to eat
ex: Many children suffer from hunger.
He ate quickly to satisfy his hunger.

senses.def: a search for someone or something
ex: The police began a hunt for the thief.
I'm on a job hunt.

senses.def: to chase and kill animals for food or sport
ex: Lions hunt at night.
They hunt deer in the forest.

senses.def: to look carefully for someone or something
ex: I hunted for my keys everywhere.

senses.def: a person or animal that hunts
ex: The hunter followed the tracks of a deer.

senses.def: the activity of chasing and killing animals
ex: Hunting is banned in this area.
He loves hunting and fishing.

senses.def: the activity of looking for something
ex: House hunting can take months.

senses.def: the need to do something quickly
ex: I can't talk now, I'm in a hurry.
There's no hurry.

senses.def: to move or do something quickly because you have little time
ex: Hurry up, or we'll miss the bus.
She hurried home.

senses.def: to cause pain or injury to someone or yourself, or to feel pain
ex: I hurt my leg playing football.
My back hurts.

senses.def: to make someone feel sad or upset
ex: His words hurt her deeply.

senses.def: injured, or feeling sad because of what someone has said or done
ex: Three people were hurt in the crash.
She felt hurt by his answer.

senses.def: the man that a woman is married to
ex: Her husband works in a bank.
They met when her husband was a student.

senses.def: to tell someone to be quiet, or to become quiet
ex: She hushed the baby.
Hush! The baby is asleep.

senses.def: a small, simple building, often made of wood
ex: They spent the night in a mountain hut.

senses.def: made from two or more different things combined
ex: He drives a hybrid car.
The company has a hybrid working model.

senses.def: the practice of keeping yourself and things around you clean to stop disease
ex: Good hygiene stops germs from spreading.
Wash your hands for personal hygiene.

senses.def: pretending to have beliefs or values that you do not really have
ex: People criticised the politician's hypocrisy.
It's pure hypocrisy to say one thing and do another.

senses.def: a person who says they believe in something but behaves in a different way
ex: He is a hypocrite: he tells us to save water but wastes it.

senses.def: saying you believe one thing but behaving in a different way
ex: It's hypocritical to complain about litter and then drop it.
She felt his advice was hypocritical.

senses.def: an idea or explanation that is suggested and then tested to see if it is true
ex: Scientists tested the hypothesis in the laboratory.
The data supports our hypothesis.

senses.def: based on an imagined situation rather than on real facts
ex: Let's discuss a hypothetical case.
This is only a hypothetical question.

senses.def: extreme fear or excitement that people cannot control
ex: The news caused panic and hysteria in the city.
There was mass hysteria at the concert.

senses.def: so afraid, excited or angry that you cannot control yourself
ex: The hysterical crowd rushed to the stage.
She became hysterical when she heard the news.

senses.def: extremely funny (informal)
ex: The show was absolutely hysterical.

senses.def: in a way that shows you cannot control your feelings
ex: She was laughing hysterically.
The child screamed hysterically.
